rubric.why: Credits the main diaphragm and pressure changes that cause inhalation.
rubric.description: Explains inhalation through diaphragm movement and changes in chest-cavity volume and pressure.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining that the diaphragm contracts and flattens, increasing chest-cavity volume and lowering pressure so air enters the lungs. Award 1 mark if the explanation is incomplete.

rubric.why: Credits the rib-cage movement that helps expand the chest during inhalation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the intercostal muscles contract and move the ribs upwards and outwards.

rubric.why: Credits the main diaphragm and pressure changes that cause exhalation.
rubric.description: Explains exhalation through diaphragm movement and changes in chest-cavity volume and pressure.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the diaphragm relaxes and becomes dome-shaped, decreasing chest-cavity volume and raising pressure so air is pushed out.

rubric.why: Credits the rib-cage movement during exhalation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the intercostal muscles relax and the ribs move downwards and inwards.

modelAnswer: During inhalation, the external intercostal muscles contract and move the ribs upwards and outwards.
The diaphragm contracts and flattens, increasing the volume of the chest cavity and lowering its pressure; air enters the lungs.
During exhalation, the intercostal muscles relax and the ribs move downwards and inwards.
The diaphragm relaxes and becomes dome-shaped, decreasing the volume of the chest cavity and raising its pressure; air is pushed out of the lungs.

items.followUp: What is a parasite? Give one example of a parasite and its host.

rubric.why: Credits the definition of a parasite as an organism that lives on or inside a host and obtains nourishment from it.
rubric.description: Defines a parasite in relation to its host and source of nourishment.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a parasite lives on or inside another organism (its host) and obtains nourishment or food from it.

rubric.why: Credits a valid example of a parasite.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a parasite.
rubric.how: Award for any correct example, such as tapeworm, Plasmodium, lice, roundworm or leech.

modelAnswer: A parasite is an organism that lives on or inside another organism, called its host, and obtains nourishment from it.
Examples of parasites include tapeworm and Plasmodium.
